title: Lipid Lab
desc: CHEM 3B lipid practice: identify fatty acids from drawn chains (saturation, shorthand, omega, melting point), build and break triacylglycerols (esterification, hydrolysis, saponification, hydrogenation), classify lipids from their structures, work membrane and transport questions, and connect lipids to the clinic, plus final-exam practice.

subtitle: Fatty acids, fats and oils, phospholipids, steroids and membranes: read the chains, build the esters, break them back down.
tip: Count carbons from the carboxyl end for IUPAC numbers and from the CH<sub>3</sub> end for omega numbers; every cis double bond is a kink that lowers the melting point.
reference:
🧠 Reference: fatty acids and lipid classes
Fatty acidShorthandOmegaMelting pointFound in
Lauric12:0—44 °Ccoconut oil
Myristic14:0—54 °Cnutmeg, butter
Palmitic16:0—63 °Cpalm oil, most fats
Stearic18:0—70 °Canimal fat, cocoa butter
Oleic18:1 (Δ9)ω-913 °Colive oil
Linoleic (essential)18:2 (Δ9,12)ω-6−5 °Ccorn, soybean oil
α-Linolenic (essential)18:3 (Δ9,12,15)ω-3−11 °Cflax, walnuts
Arachidonic20:4ω-6−49 °Cmade from linoleic; prostaglandin parent
EPA / DHA20:5 / 22:6ω-3below −50 °Cfish oil

Classes: triacylglycerols (glycerol + 3 fatty acids; saponifiable) · glycerophospholipids (glycerol + 2 fatty acids + phosphate + alcohol such as choline) · sphingolipids (sphingosine + 1 fatty acid by an amide + phosphate/choline or a sugar) · steroids (four fused rings: cholesterol, bile salts, hormones, vitamin D) · waxes (fatty acid + long alcohol ester) · eicosanoids (prostaglandins, from arachidonic acid). Lipoproteins by rising density: chylomicron → VLDL → LDL → HDL.
